notes: City of Vancouver, BC (Canada) Open Data Portal (opendata.vancouver.ca, OpenDataSoft). Geometry from 'property-parcel-polygons' (already city-scoped, no boundary clip needed); values from 'property-tax-report' latest report_year, joined on tax_coord/land_coordinate. Both open, no gating. See data/jurisidictions/run_vancouverbc.py for the full sourcing writeup, the strata-sum aggregation rule (verified live: per-unit land value is a genuine proportionate share, not a duplicated broadcast), and the exemption-by-absence handling (untaxed government/park/crown land simply has no tax-report row).

origCategoryField is zoning_classification (BC Assessment's actual-use code is not published in this open extract, so zoning is the best available land-use proxy — it is a legal-use bucket, not true use).

hideUnderutilized is true: the default land-share classifier flags ~95% of parcels as 'Underdeveloped' (vs ~33% in Seattle) because Vancouver land value is famously and genuinely far larger than improvement value even for ordinary single-family homes (median improvement value is only ~12% of land value citywide). That's a real market feature, not a data bug, but it makes the tab non-discriminating, so it's hidden per Greg's call (2026-08-20).

93,409 parcels -> PMTiles + H3 hexes (parquet_to_pmtiles.py), right at the ~100k rule-of-thumb threshold; baked given the city's profile. parcels z12-14, parcels_low (H3) z0-11, parcels_under z1-14 — all three layers verified present.
Currency is CAD; currencySymbol 'CA$' to distinguish from the USD cities.
